note: Candidate definitions for SV-META (spec sections 6-9). Written by the package agent from the census, out/themes.csv and the novelty search (CB notes and texts, SV-G2 rows, PubMed). Numbers are quoted from out/themes.csv or the census; screen.py and build_load.py read them from the files, this file holds the judgement.

candidates.label: Higher circulating monocyte count in more severe disease (with CD14 and CCL2 as supporting markers)
candidates.circularity: none (no monocyte variable in any label)
candidates.novelty_where: CCL2 by outcome published per cohort (CB517, CB017); CD14 by complicated status (CB112); monocyte activation proposed as a mechanism (CB107, CB119, CB517); CCL2 also published in an independent B. rossi cohort (CB037). No CB article combines independent sources, and the DS05 (Eastern Cape) monocyte association is unpublished. The sCD14/presepsin parallel is not made in a CB text found
candidates.sources: SRC-A, SRC-B, SRC-C, SRC-F (B. rossi); SRC-D (B. canis, transfer)
candidates.evidence: T02 B. rossi 4 of 4 sources in the expected direction, Stouffer one-sided p 4e-05, BH q 0.00016 over 8 themes (themes chosen after results were seen), leave-one-source-out max p 0.0105; with SRC-D 5 of 5
candidates.screen_reason: no single non-published source passes alone except SRC-F (DS05 monocytes with dullness, already seen); convergent across 4 B. rossi sources

candidates.label: Inflammation against regeneration at a given haematocrit (SV-09 residual axis 2) tracks dullness
candidates.circularity: none (habitus is not a laboratory label); partly restates leukocytes
candidates.novelty_where: inadequate regeneration and cytokine-suppressed erythropoiesis proposed in CB115, CB129, CB082, with the malaria parallel (CB129, CB115); no CB article links it to clinical severity
candidates.evidence: partial rho with habitus -0.26 (-0.40 to -0.10), p 0.003, family of 2 axes, n 140 (DS05, already seen: exploratory)
candidates.screen_reason: passes the statistical screen in one source; not replicable in other files (SV-09-02)

candidates.label: Intravascular haemolysis per unit of anaemia (cell-free haemoglobin, haem scavenging)
candidates.circularity: partial: DS07 label contains haematocrit < 0.15 and bilirubin > 30
candidates.novelty_where: SV-06a F1-01 measured_no_severity (CB082, CB412); haem oxygenase-1 never measured; haemopexin and haptoglobin measured without severity
candidates.evidence: T04: DS07 haemoglobin beta +0.48 (+0.09 to +0.82), q 0.133; DS02 cfHb change high vs low dose +1.0 (exact p 0.2); Stouffer p 0.005, q 0.010, leave-one-source-out fails (max p 0.1), so not tier C
candidates.screen_reason: combined test passes but leave-one-source-out fails with 2 sources; gap lead by SV-06a

candidates.label: Neutrophil degranulation and extracellular traps (NETs, histones, released MPO and elastase, calprotectin)
candidates.circularity: none for the released markers; bands are a known driver
candidates.novelty_where: SV-06a ranks 3, 4, 5, 9: never measured in canine babesiosis; band neutrophils and MPXI are published (CB050, CB040)
candidates.evidence: SV-08 neutrophil-granule score rose in 5 of 5 Beagles (also in mild dogs; MPO, ELANE missing); DS07 S100A8 +0.43 (-0.10 to +0.93), q 0.29; histone H4 untestable
candidates.screen_reason: gap lead by SV-06a; the existing data are within-dog changes or underpowered

candidates.label: Angiopoietin-2 and the Ang-2/Ang-1 ratio
candidates.novelty_where: SV-06a rank 1, never measured in canine babesiosis
candidates.evidence: SV-06a grade 3 (6 human cohorts), validated canine assay
candidates.screen_reason: gap lead

candidates.label: VWF, ultra-large multimers and ADAMTS13
candidates.novelty_where: SV-06a rank 6, measured only against controls (CB446)
candidates.evidence: SV-06a grade 3 (4 human cohorts), validated canine assay
candidates.screen_reason: gap lead

candidates.label: VEGF and soluble VEGFR-1 (sFlt-1)
candidates.novelty_where: SV-06a rank 2, never measured
candidates.evidence: SV-06a grade 3 (4 human cohorts), validated canine VEGF assay
candidates.screen_reason: gap lead

candidates.label: Ferritin (hyperferritinaemia)
candidates.novelty_where: SV-06a rank 7, measured, no difference 7 vs 7 (CB242)
candidates.evidence: SV-06a grade 3 (4 human cohorts), validated canine assay
candidates.screen_reason: gap lead

candidates.label: Kynurenine pathway (kynurenine:tryptophan)
candidates.novelty_where: SV-06a rank 8, measured against controls in B. canis (CB091)
candidates.evidence: SV-06a grade 3 (4 human cohorts), validated canine assay
candidates.screen_reason: gap lead

candidates.label: Neutrophil activation and left shift (band neutrophils, lactoferrin)
candidates.circularity: known_driver (bands); label in SRC-C and SRC-D
candidates.novelty_where: band neutrophils with death published (CB050, CB040); lactoferrin with complicated status (CB112)
candidates.evidence: T01 B. rossi Stouffer Z 5.23, 3 of 3, leave-one-source-out max p 0.0001
candidates.screen_reason: strong convergence, but band neutrophils are a published severity finding and a declared known driver; the SRC-C and SRC-D indicators are in their labels

candidates.label: CCL2 (MCP-1) higher in severe disease in each file
candidates.novelty_where: CB517 (S-CB050 dogs) and CB017 (S-CB017 dogs); the malaria and sepsis parallel is made in CB017, CB517 and CB107
candidates.screen_reason: each per-file result is the published finding of the article that reported those dogs; it is carried into K01 only as a sensitivity

candidates.label: GM-CSF and IL-2 higher in complicated B. canis
candidates.novelty_where: CB017 (SV-G2 rows: GM-CSF p 0.00066, IL-2 p 0.025 on day 1)
candidates.screen_reason: passes in one source, but it is the published finding of CB017; no B. rossi counterpart

candidates.label: Type 1 interferon transcript response in the Beagles
candidates.novelty_where: type I IFN genes reported in the same Beagles (CB082) and cited in CB111
candidates.evidence: rose in 5 of 5 dogs, before habitus fell; dose contrast -0.67 (low-dose dogs rose more); no severity gradient
candidates.screen_reason: a response to infection already reported for these dogs; the severe-malaria parallel (inadequate suppression of type 1 IFN, 10.1126/scitranslmed.aar3619) cannot be tested in 5 dogs

candidates.label: Anaemia (haematocrit)
candidates.circularity: known_driver; label in SRC-C and SRC-D
candidates.novelty_where: anaemia is a defining feature (SV-03 haematocrit 23 units)
candidates.evidence: T07 Stouffer p 0.0001, but leave-one-source-out max p 0.1
candidates.screen_reason: known driver by the spec

candidates.label: Anti-inflammatory IL-10
candidates.novelty_where: IL-10/TNF severity-tested in 5 canine units (SV-06a F7-01)
candidates.evidence: T11 2 of 2 (3 of 3 with B. canis), Stouffer p 0.081, q 0.13
candidates.screen_reason: combined q 0.13

candidates.label: Coagulation and platelet consumption
candidates.novelty_where: CB145 (Onderstepoort, factor activities by outcome)
candidates.evidence: T05 1 of 3 in the expected direction, Stouffer p 0.68
candidates.screen_reason: directions disagree; null

candidates.label: Host age
candidates.novelty_where: age tested in 12 literature units (SV-G2)
candidates.screen_reason: null; only large effects were detectable

candidates.label: Acute phase response (CRP)
candidates.novelty_where: no outcome difference in CB517 and CB145
candidates.evidence: T13 1 of 2, Stouffer p 0.66
candidates.screen_reason: null

candidates.label: Size of the cytokine response (perturbation count)
candidates.screen_reason: passes only in the source whose label contains SIRS

candidates.label: SV-09 leukocyte axis score with death
candidates.novelty_where: band neutrophils with death (CB050)
candidates.screen_reason: restates band neutrophils

candidates.label: Distance from the Beagle course (SV-01)
candidates.evidence: H1 -0.24 (-0.39 to -0.07); +0.08 once haematocrit is controlled; stage score failed validation
candidates.screen_reason: restates anaemia; the stage score failed validation and is unstable

candidates.label: Antibody level against load (CB141, B. canis)
candidates.novelty_where: CB141
candidates.evidence: antibody rho -0.65 (-0.73 to -0.56), load rho 0.35 (0.23 to 0.46)
candidates.screen_reason: published single cohort; the test needs dog-level data (SV-02c, a user decision)

candidates.label: Endocrine stress response (cortisol up, thyroid down), body temperature
candidates.novelty_where: CB040, CB342, CH09; all Onderstepoort
candidates.evidence: 3 of 3 units each (post hoc merged classes); 2 units once Onderstepoort is counted once
candidates.screen_reason: published and from one hospital

candidates.label: Lactate
candidates.circularity: label in SRC-C and several definitions
candidates.novelty_where: CB040, CB516, CH18; human parallel made in the CB literature
candidates.evidence: 3 units higher in death (SV-03); Beagles high vs low dose +1.0
candidates.screen_reason: published severity marker

candidates.label: Young dogs present earlier (DS05)
candidates.screen_reason: q 0.09 in its family

candidates.label: MCP-1 minus IL-8 balance index
candidates.screen_reason: carried by MCP-1; fails the correction in S-CB050

candidates.label: Parasite load
candidates.evidence: CB516 g -0.17 (-1.19 to 0.85); no B. rossi load-by-outcome unit
candidates.screen_reason: null in the one dog-level contrast; no B. rossi data

candidates.label: Infected against healthy controls (IL-8 direction, MCP-1, IL-10, CD14, antithrombin)
candidates.evidence: e.g. IL-8 -0.45 in S-CB050 and +0.87 in S-CB017
candidates.screen_reason: infection response, not severity; reported in the source articles; a between-file difference cannot be attributed to species

candidates.label: Lower haematocrit in young infected Onderstepoort dogs (DS03)
candidates.screen_reason: the normal age difference explains part of it; not seen in the independent source

leads.hypothesis: In B. rossi babesiosis, a higher circulating monocyte count at admission goes with more severe disease, beyond anaemia and total leukocytes.
leads.evidence: T02: 4 of 4 B. rossi sources in the expected direction (DS05 monocytes with dullness rho +0.45, partial +0.29 after haematocrit, WBC, segmented and band neutrophils and illness days; S-CB517 died +0.25; DS07 CD14 +0.42, halves after haemoglobin beta; Beagles +0.67), Stouffer q 0.00016 over 8 themes; but without DS05, the source that suggested it, Z 2.31 (Bonferroni 0.084). Monocyte count does not track MCP-1
leads.human_counterpart: Monocyte/macrophage markers with severity: soluble CD14 with severity in falciparum malaria and presepsin (sCD14-ST) higher in sepsis non-survivors agree; MCP-1 independently prognostic in sepsis; but monocyte activation markers were lower in severe malaria in Malawian children and MCP-1 lower in complicated falciparum malaria (mixed)
leads.parallel_new: partly: the CCL2 (MCP-1) parallel is made in CB017, CB517, CB107; a circulating monocyte count or sCD14 parallel was not found in a CB text
leads.refuted_by: No monocyte-count difference by outcome in a non-Onderstepoort B. rossi cohort with a hard outcome, or a difference that disappears after WBC and haematocrit adjustment
leads.next_existing: Monocyte count and monocyte fraction against death in the probable DS03-S-CB050 join is not possible (DS03 has no leukocytes); cheapest: ask the CB040 authors (320 B. rossi dogs, SV-02c request) for dog-level monocyte counts and outcome
leads.next_new_dogs: SV-10-03 prospective B. rossi cohort with at least 200 dogs outside Onderstepoort: admission CBC with differential, outcome components stored separately
leads.minimum_dataset: Manual or analyser differential with absolute monocyte count; plasma sCD14 (presepsin) and CCL2 on stored pre-treatment plasma
leads.refuted_short: No monocyte difference by outcome in a non-Onderstepoort cohort, or none after WBC and haematocrit adjustment
leads.existing_short: Ask the CB040 authors (320 dogs) for monocyte counts and outcome (SV-02c)
leads.md_short: Absolute monocyte count; plasma sCD14 and CCL2

leads.hypothesis: More intravascular haemolysis per unit of anaemia (cell-free haemoglobin and haem load relative to haematocrit and scavenger capacity) goes with severe and fatal B. rossi disease, as in severe falciparum and knowlesi malaria and sepsis.
leads.evidence: Gap: no CB article relates measured cell-free haemoglobin or haem to outcome. Existing data do not support it: DS07 haemoglobin beta +0.48 (q 0.133) partly restates the label and moves with another red-cell protein (sample haemolysis not excluded); the Beagle cfHb contrast is parasite load, already reported (CB082)
leads.human_counterpart: Cell-free haemoglobin higher with AKI in severe falciparum malaria, with death in Ugandan children (with low haemopexin), with severity in knowlesi malaria, and independently with death in sepsis
leads.parallel_new: partly: CB119 proposes cfHb as a severity measure without data; no quantified canine cfHb-outcome study
leads.refuted_by: No difference in cfHb (or cfHb per haematocrit unit, or haemopexin depletion) between dogs that die and survive in a cohort that measures a sample haemolysis index
leads.next_existing: None adequate: DS07 lacks haematocrit, bilirubin and a haemolysis index. Cheapest is stored pre-treatment plasma (CB145 / Onderstepoort biobank, SV-02c-type request)
leads.next_new_dogs: SV-10-03 cohort: plasma cfHb by spectrophotometry with haematocrit, haptoglobin, haemopexin and a haemolysis index at admission
leads.minimum_dataset: Plasma cell-free haemoglobin, haemolysis index, haptoglobin, haemopexin; urine haemoglobin
leads.canine_line: No canine study relates measured cell-free haemoglobin to outcome. DS07 haemoglobin beta (q 0.133) partly restates the label; the Beagle contrast is parasite load
leads.refuted_short: No cfHb difference by outcome when a haemolysis index is measured
leads.new_short: SV-10-03 cohort with haematocrit, haptoglobin, haemopexin
leads.md_short: Plasma cfHb, haemolysis index, haptoglobin, haemopexin

leads.hypothesis: Neutrophil degranulation and extracellular trap release (cfDNA, nucleosomes, histones, released MPO and elastase, calprotectin) are greater in severe B. rossi babesiosis, beyond neutrophil number.
leads.evidence: Gap: never measured in canine babesiosis (CB107 states NETosis is unstudied). Weak, confounded support: DS07 S100A8 +0.43 (q 0.29), a third explained by haemoglobin beta; histone H4 untestable; Beagle granule transcripts rose in all 5 dogs with no severity gradient
leads.human_counterpart: Plasma elastase and MPO higher in cerebral malaria; circulating histones raised with brain swelling in cerebral malaria; neutrophil granule transcripts associated with severe malaria and with sepsis mortality; but cfDNA and MPO-DNA did not predict death after adjustment in a sepsis cohort (mixed)
leads.parallel_new: yes for NETs, histones, calprotectin and released MPO/elastase (only speculated in CB articles); band neutrophils and MPXI are published
leads.refuted_by: Plasma cfDNA, nucleosomes or calprotectin no higher in dogs that die once the band neutrophil count is adjusted for
leads.next_existing: Re-quantify DS06 from SRA PRJNA703846 without the CPM filter to recover MPO and ELANE (a coordinator decision, large download); no severity contrast in those 5 dogs
leads.next_new_dogs: SV-10-03 cohort: citrate plasma (not serum) for cfDNA by fluorometry and calprotectin; nucleosome ELISA only with a haemolysis and icterus check
leads.minimum_dataset: Plasma cfDNA, calprotectin (S100A8/A9), plasma MPO and elastase; band and segmented neutrophil counts
leads.canine_line: Never measured in canine babesiosis. Nearest data: DS07 S100A8 +0.43 (q 0.29) and a Beagle granule-transcript rise with no severity gradient
leads.refuted_short: cfDNA, nucleosomes or calprotectin no higher in dogs that die, after band neutrophils
leads.existing_short: Re-quantify DS06 from SRA (MPO, ELANE); no severity contrast
leads.md_short: cfDNA, calprotectin, plasma MPO and elastase

leads.hypothesis: Endothelial activation measured as plasma angiopoietin-2 is higher in dogs with severe or fatal B. rossi babesiosis.
leads.evidence: Gap: never measured in canine babesiosis (0 CB notes or texts, 1 PubMed record not about Ang-2). Not in DS07; DS06 holds no ANGPT2 transcript. The Ang-2/Ang-1 ratio is not assayable in dogs with the validated kit, so the lead is Ang-2 alone
leads.human_counterpart: Ang-2 rose with severity in all 11 falciparum studies of a systematic review and discriminated death (AUROC 0.71 to 0.83); higher in sepsis non-survivors (meta-analysis); in canine SIRS and sepsis higher in non-survivors
leads.parallel_new: yes: no CB article makes it
leads.refuted_by: No Ang-2 difference between dogs that die and survive once haemolysis and creatinine are accounted for
leads.next_existing: None in the public files. Stored pre-treatment plasma with outcome (Onderstepoort biobank; contacting the authors is a user decision)
leads.next_new_dogs: SV-10-03 cohort: plasma Ang-2 at admission with creatinine and a haemolysis index
leads.minimum_dataset: Plasma angiopoietin-2 (validated canine ELISA), stored EDTA or citrate plasma at -80 C
leads.canine_line: Never measured in canine babesiosis; not in any public file
leads.refuted_short: No Ang-2 difference by outcome after haemolysis and creatinine

leads.hypothesis: VWF release and ADAMTS13 consumption (a higher VWF:ADAMTS13 ratio) go with severe B. rossi babesiosis and its microthrombi.
leads.evidence: Gap: CB145 measured factor activities, fibrinolysis and microthrombi at necropsy by outcome, but not VWF or ADAMTS13; CB446 found vWF activity lower than in controls in 12 dogs without an outcome contrast, so the direction cannot be assumed. Coagulation theme T05 null (1 of 3)
leads.human_counterpart: Higher VWF and ultra-large multimers with lower ADAMTS13 in severe and cerebral falciparum malaria (small cohorts); VWF in malaria-associated ARDS
leads.parallel_new: yes for the severity link; CB446 measured vWF against controls only
leads.refuted_by: VWF antigen, VWF activity and ADAMTS13 activity the same in dogs that die and survive, or VWF lower in severe dogs as CB446's direction suggests
leads.next_existing: None public. CB145 cohort plasma (thromboinflammation study, raw data on request) is the natural place to add VWF and ADAMTS13
leads.next_new_dogs: SV-10-03 cohort: citrate plasma for VWF antigen, VWF:collagen binding and ADAMTS13 activity
leads.minimum_dataset: Citrate plasma: VWF antigen, VWF activity, ADAMTS13 activity; platelet count
leads.canine_line: Not measured against severity; CB446 found vWF activity lower than in controls (12 dogs)
leads.refuted_short: VWF and ADAMTS13 the same in dogs that die and survive, or VWF lower
leads.existing_short: Add to the CB145 cohort plasma (on request)
leads.md_short: VWF antigen and activity, ADAMTS13 activity

leads.hypothesis: Hyperferritinaemia (macrophage activation and iron sequestration) at admission goes with severe or fatal B. rossi babesiosis.
leads.evidence: Gap: the only canine babesiosis ferritin data are 7 infected vs 7 healthy dogs (CB242, no severity contrast, species not identified) and one case report. Not in DS07 or any tidy file. Confounded in a haemolytic disease by iron release and the acute-phase response
leads.human_counterpart: Ferritin higher in sepsis non-survivors in several large cohorts; very high ferritin marks a macrophage-activation-like phenotype in septic shock; in malaria ferritin rises with clinical infection but is confounded by inflammation (an infection contrast, not severity)
leads.parallel_new: yes: no CB article makes it
leads.refuted_by: No ferritin difference by outcome once CRP and a haemolysis marker (cell-free haemoglobin or bilirubin) are adjusted for
leads.next_existing: None public; stored serum with outcome (same biobank question as the other plasma leads)
leads.next_new_dogs: SV-10-03 cohort: serum ferritin with CRP, serum iron and transferrin at admission
leads.minimum_dataset: Serum ferritin (canine immunoassay), with CRP, serum iron, transferrin and a haemolysis marker
leads.canine_line: Only 7 infected vs 7 healthy dogs (CB242), no severity contrast
leads.refuted_short: No ferritin difference by outcome after CRP and a haemolysis marker
leads.md_short: Serum ferritin with CRP, iron, transferrin

leads.hypothesis: Higher kynurenine:tryptophan (IDO activity) at admission goes with severe or fatal canine babesiosis.
leads.evidence: Gap: kynurenine was measured only against healthy dogs (CB091 serum, B. canis: kynurenine and Kyn/Trp clearly higher in infected dogs, no severity label). The nearest severity proxy (CB071 urine, renal-function groups, 5 to 10 dogs per group) is null. CB071, CB091 and CB137 are one cohort (CH06)
leads.human_counterpart: Higher IDO activity (kynurenine:tryptophan) and kynurenine with sepsis severity and death; CSF kynurenine pathway metabolites with longer coma in cerebral malaria (mostly cerebral, not systemic, evidence in malaria)
leads.parallel_new: yes for severity; the infection contrast is published (CB091)
leads.refuted_by: No Kyn/Trp difference by outcome once creatinine (azotaemia) and CRP are adjusted for
leads.next_existing: None public with a severity label; the CB091 supplement has dog-level values but no severity label (ask the authors for complicated status: a user decision)
leads.next_new_dogs: SV-10-03 cohort: plasma tryptophan and kynurenine by LC-MS/MS with creatinine and CRP
leads.minimum_dataset: Plasma tryptophan, kynurenine (LC-MS/MS); creatinine and CRP for adjustment
leads.canine_line: Measured only against healthy dogs (CB091, B. canis); no severity label
leads.refuted_short: No Kyn/Trp difference by outcome after creatinine and CRP
leads.existing_short: Ask the CB091 authors for complicated status
